summary: Middle-aged woman with a large painful right anterior abdominal wall desmoid tumor (biopsy-proven, previously 14 cm) admitted overnight after staged CT/ultrasound-guided cryoablation of the residual tumor. The procedure was uncomplicated; she was observed for post-procedural right-sided abdominal/flank pain and transient nausea, managed with dilaudid PCA, IV ketorolac and IV ondansetron, then transitioned to oral agents. Labs show a reactive post-ablation leukocytosis (WBC 12.5 → 15.2) and thrombocytosis without evidence of infection or bleeding; chronic hepatitis C (genotype 3, VL ~430,000) was unchanged inpatient.
most_likely: Desmoid tumor (aggressive fibromatosis) of anterior abdominal wall, neoplasm of uncertain behavior of soft tissue, status post cryoablation

differential.diagnosis: Desmoid tumor (aggressive fibromatosis) of anterior abdominal wall — neoplasm of uncertain behavior of connective/soft tissue
supporting_evidence: CT: residual large right abdominal wall desmoid tumor cryoablated
Prior stay principal ICD-10 D48.1 for same lesion
opposing_evidence: Admission mechanism was post-procedure observation rather than tumor complication
differential.reasoning: The disease driving this planned staged-ablation admission is the residual abdominal wall desmoid tumor; it is the billable principal condition rather than the procedural event.

differential.diagnosis: Acute post-procedural (post-ablation) abdominal pain requiring parenteral analgesia
supporting_evidence: Post-procedural right abdominal pain radiating to back on floor exam
Managed with dilaudid PCA and IV toradol overnight
Prior admission coded G89.18 for identical scenario
differential.reasoning: Pain control was the explicit reason for the overnight stay and is well documented, making it a strong secondary/complication code.

differential.diagnosis: Post-procedural nausea following general anesthesia and cryoablation
supporting_evidence: 'one brief episode of nausea that then passed', no vomiting
Treated with IV Zofran, discharged on prochlorperazine
opposing_evidence: Nausea mild and self-limited this admission, unlike prior stay with emesis
differential.reasoning: Documented and treated symptom of the current stay, but milder than the prior admission so scored below pain.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic hepatitis C virus infection, genotype 3, with hepatic fibrosis
supporting_evidence: FibroScan consistent with fibrosis; prior ICD B18.2
opposing_evidence: No inpatient management or hepatic decompensation this stay
differential.reasoning: Active chronic comorbidity explicitly addressed in the hospital course ('no changes as inpatient'), supporting a secondary code.

differential.diagnosis: Reactive leukocytosis secondary to tissue ablation and inflammatory response
supporting_evidence: WBC 12.5 on admission rising to 15.2 at discharge; platelets 484
Prior stay WBC 19.4 attributed to post-procedure inflammation
opposing_evidence: Afebrile, no infectious signs, no antibiotics given
differential.reasoning: Objective abnormal lab likely inflammatory/post-ablation; clinically non-actionable but codable as an abnormal finding.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic pain due to abdominal wall neoplasm on long-term opioid therapy
supporting_evidence: History of large painful desmoid with home oxycodone and Sulindac
Prior stay coded G89.29 chronic pain
opposing_evidence: Current documentation emphasizes acute post-procedural rather than baseline pain
differential.reasoning: Baseline tumor-related chronic pain contextualizes analgesic needs but is secondary to the acute post-procedural pain this stay.

supporting_evidence: Prior coding E66.9 with BMI Z-code
opposing_evidence: Not discussed in current note text
differential.reasoning: Objectively documented BMI supports an obesity plus BMI code as a comorbidity/risk factor.

supporting_evidence: PMH lists thyroiditis; prior FNA consistent with Hashimoto thyroiditis
opposing_evidence: No thyroid labs or treatment this admission
differential.reasoning: Stable chronic comorbidity carried from PMH with no current activity, hence a low score.

differential.diagnosis: Post-procedural hemorrhage or hematoma of abdominal wall
supporting_evidence: Hemoglobin fell 12.7 to 11.2; right-sided abdominal tenderness
opposing_evidence: Report states hemostasis achieved, no immediate complications
Hemodynamically stable, drop consistent with IV fluid dilution
differential.reasoning: Considered because of the modest hemoglobin decline, but imaging and stable vitals argue strongly against clinically significant bleeding.

rule_outs.why: Afebrile with normal vitals and no antibiotics; leukocytosis attributed to ablation-induced inflammation

rule_outs.diagnosis: Bowel injury or perforation from cryoprobe placement
rule_outs.why: Soft abdomen without rebound or guarding; post-ablation CT showed normal intra-abdominal organs

rule_outs.diagnosis: Malignant soft tissue sarcoma of abdominal wall
rule_outs.why: Lesion is biopsy-proven desmoid (locally aggressive, uncertain behavior), not malignant sarcoma
Creatinine 0.5, normal electrolytes, no myoglobinuria documented

uncertain_areas: Whether the coder assigns the desmoid neoplasm or acute post-procedural pain as principal for this observation stay
Absence of CRP/fever curve leaves inflammatory vs infectious cause of rising WBC unproven
Exact fibrosis stage of hepatitis C (cirrhosis vs fibrosis) would change comorbidity severity coding
Whether nausea was formally documented as post-procedural vomiting (R11.2) or nausea alone (R11.0)
